parameters.command:
=BASE=/projects/migration-{{ $('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.job_id }}
SLN=$(find $BASE -name '*.sln' | head -1)
echo '=== CVE DEPENDENCY AUDIT ==='
if [ -n "$SLN" ]; then
  dotnet list "$SLN" package --vulnerable --include-transitive 2>&1 || echo 'AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE'
else
  find $BASE -name '*.csproj' | head -5 | while read f; do
    dotnet list "$f" package --vulnerable --include-transitive 2>&1
  done
fi
echo 'CVE_CHECK_COMPLETE'

=BASE=/projects/migration-{{ $('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.job_id }}
SLN=$(find $BASE -name '*.sln' | head -1)
FILTER='Category!=DatabaseTest&Category!=IntegrationTest'
TARGET="$SLN"
if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  TARGET=$(find $BASE \( -name '*.Tests.csproj' -o -name '*Tests.csproj' \) | head -1)
fi
if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  echo 'NO_TEST_PROJECT_FOUND'
  exit 0
fi
OUT=$(dotnet test "$TARGET" --filter "$FILTER" --logger 'console;verbosity=normal' 2>&1)
CODE=$?
echo "$OUT" | tail -100
# Sentinel from the exit code, last line, so the gate never depends on wording.
if [ $CODE -ne 0 ]; then echo 'TESTS_FAILED'; else echo 'TESTS_PASSED'; fi

={{ "You are fixing build errors in a .NET repository that has just been migrated to a new target framework. You have tools that read, search and edit the files, look up Microsoft documentation, and build the project. Work until the build succeeds, then stop and summarise what you changed.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the build errors below. Group them: several errors usually share one cause.
2. If the context below lists PLANNED EDITS WHOSE INTENDED CODE IS NOT IN THE FILE, start there: that is the code the migration plan meant to produce, and it is usually the fix.
3. For each file you intend to change, call read_file FIRST. The code has already been modified by the migration, so it does not look like the original plan any more.
4. Do not guess an API. If you are unsure which namespace a type lives in, or which constructor or method exists, look it up with docs_search (Microsoft types) or grep_repo (this repository's own code and usings) before editing.
5. Make ONE edit at a time with replace_in_file and read its result before the next. Never send several edits to the same file in one step. If an edit reports FAILED, the file is unchanged - read it again and copy the current text exactly rather than guessing.
6. Fix causes, not symptoms. A missing using directive can produce a dozen CS0246 errors; add the using once.
7. After your edits, call build. It is the only way to know the fix works. If it still fails, read the new errors and continue. Never report the build as fixed unless build returned BUILD SUCCEEDED.

THE EDIT THAT WILL ACTUALLY APPLY
replace_in_file matches oldText literally against the file. It falls back to whitespace-insensitive line matching, but nothing else - it will not find a paraphrase.
Copy oldText out of what read_file returned. Include just enough surrounding code to appear exactly once in the file: a bare `public IActionResult` will match many places and fail, the same line with its method name will not. That is the whole rule - long enough to be unique, no longer.
Never send an empty oldText. To insert code, include the existing lines around the insertion point in both oldText and newText.

WHEN TO REWRITE THE WHOLE FILE
Use write_file when the errors are structural - CS1022, CS1513, CS1002, unbalanced braces, a duplicated block. A targeted edit reliably misses a trailing brace at the end of the file. Pass the complete file, top to bottom. For anything else prefer replace_in_file.

PACKAGES
Use manage_package, never a file edit, for PackageReference changes. On NU1605 (package downgrade) take the required version from the error text itself - do not invent one. Microsoft.NETCore.App and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App are implicit framework references, not packages; adding them breaks the build.

PATHS
Build output shows absolute paths like /projects/migration-42/Utils/Thing.cs. Always pass the repo-relative path: Utils/Thing.cs. Only files in the REPOSITORY FILES list below exist - never request any other path, and if read_file answers NOT FOUND, do not ask for that path again.

TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE FIXES AND ARE NOT
- A TODO comment, an empty method body or a swallowed exception makes the build pass while removing behaviour. If you genuinely cannot fix something, say so in your summary and leave it.
- Changing a declaration without its call sites. If you make a method async or rename it, update everything that calls it in the same pass - grep for it if you are unsure it is unused.

COMMENTS THE FIX MAKES WRONG
If a comment or an [Obsolete] attribute inside the code you are replacing describes what the old code did, rewrite or delete it in the same edit. Leaving "// WebClient is obsolete" above code that no longer uses WebClient is misleading, and a stale [Obsolete] attribute also warns at every call site.

WHEN YOU ARE DONE
Reply with a short plain-text summary: which files you changed, what each fix addressed, the result of your last build call, and anything you could not fix and why. The next attempt, if there is one, reads this summary - be accurate about what you changed. Do not output JSON.
" + '

This is attempt ' + ($runIndex + 1) + ' of 3.

TARGET FRAMEWORK: ' + ($('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.target_framework || 'net8.0') + ($('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.custom_prompt ? '

USER INSTRUCTIONS:
' + $('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.custom_prompt : '') + ($json.ef_context ? '

' + $json.ef_context : '') + '

BUILD ERRORS:
' + String($('Store Build Output').first().json.build_output || '').slice(-20000) }}

options.systemMessage: You are a .NET build-error fixer. You edit files through tools. You never output JSON.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ jobId: $('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.job_id, filePath: $json.filePath, targetContent: $json.targetContent, replacementContent: $json.replacementContent }) }}

parameters.command:
=BASE=/projects/migration-{{ $('Execute Webhook').first().json.body.job_id }}
SLN=$(find $BASE -name '*.sln' | head -1)

if [ -n "$SLN" ]; then
  OUTPUT=$(dotnet build "$SLN" 2>&1)
  STATUS=$?
else
  PROJ=$(find $BASE -name '*.csproj' | head -1)
  if [ -n "$PROJ" ]; then
    OUTPUT=$(dotnet build "$PROJ" 2>&1)
    STATUS=$?
  else
    OUTPUT="NO_PROJECT_FOUND"
    STATUS=1
  fi
fi

if [ $STATUS -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "$OUTPUT"
  # v5.3: the per-file `cat` that used to live here is gone. The Error Fixer
  # is a tool-using agent now and calls read_file for what it actually needs,
  # instead of every failing file being pasted into the prompt and staying in
  # context for the rest of the run.
  echo "BUILD_FAILED"
else
  echo "$OUTPUT"
  echo "BUILD_SUCCESS"
fi

parameters.name: read_file
parameters.description: Read a file from the repository. Call this before editing anything: the code has already been changed by the migration and no longer matches the original plan.

parameters.name: replace_in_file
parameters.description: Replace an exact snippet in a file. oldText must be copied from what read_file returned and must appear exactly once. Reports whether it applied, so check the result before the next edit.

parameters.name: write_file
parameters.description: Overwrite a whole file. Use only for structural damage - unbalanced braces, CS1022/CS1513/CS1002, a duplicated block - where a targeted edit would miss a trailing brace. Pass the complete file.

parameters.name: manage_package
parameters.description: Add, re-pin or remove a PackageReference in a .csproj. Use this instead of editing the csproj by hand. On NU1605 take the version from the error text.

parameters.name: docs_search
parameters.description: Search official Microsoft Learn documentation. Use it before guessing a Microsoft API: which namespace a type is in, which constructors or methods exist. Returns titles, URLs and capped excerpts.

parameters.name: grep_repo
parameters.description: Search this repository for a regex or literal string and get file:line matches. Use it to find every caller of a method you change, and the using directives a file already has.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: Build the project and return the compiler errors, or BUILD SUCCEEDED. Call it after your edits: it is the only way to know a fix works. Takes about a minute.
